title: API Testing Becomes More Reliable With Validation Flows
excerpt: A successful status code isn't proof of anything. Chaining a GET after every POST, PUT, and DELETE is what actually confirms the system behaved as expected.
html:
A successful status code does not always guarantee that the system behaved correctly behind the scenes. Adding validation after every operation makes the testing process much stronger.

For example:

  • A POST request may return 201 Created, but a follow-up GET request helps confirm whether the resource was actually stored correctly.
  • An UPDATE request may return success, but another GET call is useful to verify whether the changes were truly reflected in the system.
  • A DELETE request may respond with 200 OK, yet validating with a final GET request ensures the resource is no longer available.

This approach helps verify what actually happened in the system instead of relying only on the immediate API response, because sometimes the response says everything worked while the backend data tells a different story.

Testing APIs with this kind of validation flow creates more confidence in how the application behaves in real conditions, not just how the endpoint responds during a single request.
